guides.title: Bastion Quests & Favors — Tactical Dossier
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: * Favor Level Progression: Elevating Bastion Favor unlocks passive stats (such as Crystal Mine Speed) and equips up to 2 active Bastion Skills to empower your primary KvK open-field or garrison marches.
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
⚔️ BASTION QUESTS & FAVORS GUIDE

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

* Bastion System Function: Bastions are map structures in Season of Conquest (SoC) governed by historical commanders. Completing daily Bastion Quests increases your Favor Level with that commander, yielding Crystals, Season Shop Coins, and active KvK Support Skills.

* Favor Level Progression: Elevating Bastion Favor unlocks passive stats (such as Crystal Mine Speed) and equips up to 2 active Bastion Skills to empower your primary KvK open-field or garrison marches.

* Daily Quest Cap: Players receive a limited allotment of quest completions per day (15 base, expandable via Crystal Research). Managing quest difficulty directly dictates how fast you hit max Favor level.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

* Favor Level 6 Rush Strategy: Focus 100% of your quest clears on 1 or 2 targeted Bastion Commanders until reaching Favor Level 6 to unlock their premier active skill, rather than leveling all Bastions evenly.

* Aggressive Quest Rerolling: Utilize daily free quest refreshes to immediately skip time-consuming or high-cost tasks (like train 10,000 T5 troops or defeat 10 enemy player marches).

* High-Priority Task Types: Prioritize fast, low-cost quests: Defeat Barbarians, Use Action Point Items, Harvest Resources, or Give Alliance Helps for instant Favor payouts.

* Bastion Tech Synergy: Maximize Bastion Favor I & II and Bastion Questing I & II in your Crystal Academy to boost overall Favor gained per quest while increasing total daily quest attempts.

* Resource Donating Quests: When hit with "Donate Resources to Bastion" tasks, spend raw un-tokened resources directly from your city storehouses to clear the quest instantly without burning inventory speedups.

* Kahar Whistle Stacking: Quests requiring you to "Defeat Kahar the Hidden" yield massive Season Coins and Crystals. Save Kahars to kill during active Cultural Exchange tech windows for multiplied gains.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* Match Skills to Main March: Choose Bastion Commanders whose skills complement your primary march (e.g., target Scipio/Nevsky/Zhuge-aligned Bastions for skill damage, march speed, or health buffs).

* Pre-Rally Quest Stacking: Accept "Defeat Barbarian Forts" or "Defeat Barbarians" quests right before participating in alliance fort trains to clear multiple Bastion objectives in a single sweep.

* Season Shop Coin Hoard: Exchange accumulated Season Coins earned through Bastion Favor in the KvK Shop for Legendary Equipment Blueprints, Icon Choice Chests, and Universal Sculptures.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Spreading Favor Points Evenly: Avoid leveling 4 or 5 Bastions simultaneously. Stalling at Level 2 or 3 across multiple Bastions leaves you without high-tier skill unlocks when Pass 4 war breaks out.

* Wasting Daily Quests on High-Cost Tasks: Never spend generic speedups or burn high-tier troops just to finish an inefficient Legendary-tier Bastion quest when a free refresh can provide a fast barbarian quest.

* Ignoring Idle Bastions: Do not leave your daily quest counter capped at maximum capacity; unspent daily quest attempts expire at reset, forfeiting thousands of free Crystals.

guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: * economy and cost-reduction technologies first to compound total crystal yields before investing in combat stats.
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
⚔️ CRYSTAL TECH UPGRADE PATH

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

* The Economic Foundation: Crystal Technology resets completely at the end of every Season of Conquest (SoC) season. The core objective for low spenders is to rush

* economy and cost-reduction technologies first to compound total crystal yields before investing in combat stats.

* Crystal Mine vs. Research Priority: Always keep your Crystal Mine upgrading continuously in the early weeks. Higher Mine levels increase hourly passive crystal generation, reducing your dependency on raw crystal packs.

* The Kahar & Bastion Engine: Unlocking Bastion Quests and defeating Kahars on the map provide massive crystal infusions. Economic research nodes directly scale the favor, crystals, and speedups earned from these daily activities.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

* Phase 1: Economic Rush (Pre-War Days 1–10):

* Prioritize Crystal Harvesting I and Cultural Exchange I to boost daily passive gains and Kahar drops.

* Max Crystal Research I as early as possible—this node permanently reduces the crystal cost of all subsequent technologies.

* Phase 2: Bastion & March Unlocks (Days 10–20):

* Push Bastion Favor I and Bastion Questing I to hit higher reputation levels quickly, unlocking extra skill slots and crystal quest payouts.

* Research Special Operations I to unlock your 6th (and eventually 7th) march queue for open-field combat.

* Phase 3: Targeted Combat Stats (War Preparation):

* Upgrade Marching Skill and primary troop-specific attack/health nodes (e.g., Infantry/Cavalry/Archer Tech II) strictly for your single main open-field march rather than spreading research across multiple unit types.

* Crystal Cost Discount Stacking: Never start expensive high-tier research projects without active alliance territory buffs, scientist titles, and maxed Crystal Research I/II nodes active to minimize waste.

* Kahar Chest Hoarding: Save Kahar Horns and summon chests until your Cultural Exchange research nodes are maxed to receive significantly higher crystal drops per kill.

* Crystal Supply Depot Value: Purchasing the $5 Season Pass / Crystal Supply Depot is the single highest-value purchase for low spenders, delivering steady daily crystal trickles throughout the season.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* Season Quest Milestones: Complete early Season Achievements (like defeating barbarians or clearing Bastion quests) to collect large lump-sum crystal rewards to fund Crystal Mine level jumps.

* The 1-March Combat Focus: As a low spender, focus 100% of your late-game combat research on powering up one single doom-stack march (e.g., Scipio/Liu Che) rather than splitting technology across secondary armies.

* Pre-War Reset Strategy: If you misallocate early research points into combat stats before Pass 4 opens, use a Crystal Tech Reset item to refund crystals back into economic nodes.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Rushing Combat Tech Early: Never invest heavily in Combat Tech I or troop-specific stats during the first 2 weeks; spending crystals on combat early starves your economy and halts your long-term progression.

* Ignoring Crystal Research Discount Nodes: Avoid starting high-level research tiers before maxing Crystal Research I & II, as doing so costs tens of thousands of extra crystals over the course of the season.

* Upgrading Multiple Troop Types: Do not attempt to max technology for Infantry, Cavalry, and Archers simultaneously—low-spender crystal budgets cannot sustain multi-branch combat maxing.

guides.title: KvK Healing & Resource Survival
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: * The Alliance Help Rule: Each Alliance Help received reduces active research, building, or healing timers by 1% or 3 minute minimum (depending on Alliance Center level). This mechanic makes manual healing speedups unnecessary when batching correctly.
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
⚔️ KVK HEALING & RESOURCE SURVIVAL GUIDE

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

* Hospital Capacity Hard Limit: Once your hospital reaches 100% capacity, any additional severely wounded units from open-field combat, garrisons, or rallies suffer permanent death. Monitor capacity continuously during field brawls.

* The Alliance Help Rule: Each Alliance Help received reduces active research, building, or healing timers by 1% or 3 minute minimum (depending on Alliance Center level). This mechanic makes manual healing speedups unnecessary when batching correctly.

* France Civilization Healing Buff: Switching to France prior to KvK provides a passive +20% Healing Speed boost, drastically cutting the total time required per batch.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

* Micro-Batch Healing (The 1,000–2,000 Troop Method): Select small batches of 1,000 to 2,000 troops (roughly 1 to 2 hours base healing time). Request Alliance Helps and let your alliance clear the timer instantly to heal tens of thousands of troops for zero speedups.

* Overnight Heavy Batch Queue: When logging off or sleeping, fill your entire hospital capacity with a single massive healing queue. Let passive time clear the long timer overnight without wasting Alliance Helps during peak active hours.

* Resource Reserve Shielding: Keep healing resources locked in inventory tokens. Opening hundreds of millions in food, wood, or gold in your city storehouses makes you a target for enemy raiding and burns resources through troop upkeep.

* Rune & Title Stacking: Grab a 15% Healing Speed Rune near Holy Sites and request the Doctor Title (+15% Healing Speed) from kingdom chat before initiating massive overnight or war-phase healing queues.

* VIP 10+ Healing Cost Discounts: High VIP levels grant passive healing speed bonuses and resource cost reductions for hospital operations. Reach at least VIP 10 before entering intensive KvK seasons.

* Gold Reserve Conservation: T4 and T5 infantry/cavalry/archer healing drains vast amounts of Gold. Prioritize food and wood farming on farm accounts while reserving main account gold exclusively for hospital bills.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* The Help-Button Spam Method: During active war pushes, sit in an active alliance with 30+ members online. Pop 1,500-troop healing batches every 60 seconds while continuously pressing the alliance help button to cycle fresh troops back to the field.

* Farm Account RSS Feeding: Keep 1 to 2 farm accounts parked in safe home zones. Transport raw food, wood, and gold directly to your main city via the Trading Post whenever hospital bills drain your main storage.

* Kingdom Healing Buff Activation: Coordinate with Kingdom Leaders to activate the Kingdom Healing Buff (+10% Healing Speed) during scheduled pass pushes or heavy war days.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Dumping Days of Universal Speedups on Single Queues: Never spend 30 days of Universal Speedups on a single massive 50,000-troop hospital queue in one click. Micro-batching with Alliance Helps saves those speedups for troop training events.

* Fighting with a 90%+ Full Hospital: Never re-enter open-field combat or reinforce rallies when your hospital is near maximum capacity. A single enemy AoE burst or counter-attack will cause permanent troop deaths.

* Depleting Gold Stores Early: Avoid spending gold on non-essential academy research or troop training right before KvK. Running out of gold mid-war halts hospital operations and forces your marches off the field.

guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: * Target Kingdom Status: To migrate into a kingdom, its status must be listed as Developed (or open for migration). You cannot migrate directly into a kingdom that is currently in an active Lost Kingdom (KvK) battle season or locked in Off-Season snapshot windows.
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
⚔️ KVK IMMIGRATIONS & PASSPORT GUIDE

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

* Passport Pages Requirement: Migration requires Passport Pages purchased from the Alliance Shop (600,000 Individual Credits each) or targeted real-money bundles. The total pages needed scale exponentially based on your account's current Individual Power.

* Target Kingdom Status: To migrate into a kingdom, its status must be listed as Developed (or open for migration). You cannot migrate directly into a kingdom that is currently in an active Lost Kingdom (KvK) battle season or locked in Off-Season snapshot windows.

* City Hall & Troop Conditions: You must have a City Hall Level 16+, all march queues recalled to city, zero wounded troops inside hospitals, no active alliance membership, and sufficient resource storage capacity (excess resources above storehouse limits are permanently forfeited).

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

* Migration Types (Same-Season vs. Cross-Season):

* Same-Season Migration: Moving between kingdoms within the same KvK Season/Age (e.g., Season of Conquest to Season of Conquest). Subject to standard power caps set by the target King.

* Cross-Season Migration: Moving from an older season (SoC) back to a younger season (e.g., KvK 2 or KvK 3). Highly restricted by the game engine (typically 30 spots total per kingdom per season via special King invitation).

* Targeting the Off-Season Window: Migration opens strictly during a kingdom's Off-Season window (the 10 to 14 days between the official end of one KvK and the matchmaking phase of the next).

* Power Cap Negotiation: King leadership controls the target kingdom's Special Immigration Cap. Contact the King or Migration Officer weeks in advance via mail/Discord to secure an approved spot before burning passports.

* Power Shedding (Passport Cost Reduction):

* Purge Un-Needed Troops: Fill your hospital or dismiss excess low-tier (T1–T3) or redundant troops to drop your account below major power thresholds, saving dozens of expensive Passport Pages.

* De-Equip Gear / Empty Storage: While equipment doesn't cost passports, trimming raw troop power drops your passport bracket (e.g., dropping from 65M to 55M power slashes passport costs significantly).

* Alliance Credit Stockpiling: Join high-activity alliances months before migrating. Continuously donate to alliance technology and help alliance members to farm millions of Alliance Credits for "free" passports.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* The Unassigned Spot Rush: Uncapped/uncontrolled migration spots open automatically at designated server reset times. If migrating into an open Seed C/D kingdom without a power cap, be logged in with passports ready to click instantly at reset.

* Farm Account Synchronization: Migrate your primary farm accounts along with your main city during the same Off-Season window to ensure your resource engine remains intact for the upcoming KvK.

* Kingdom Seed Assessment: Before finalizing migration, review the target kingdom's top 300 power distribution, past KvK records, and Discord organization to avoid migrating into a dead or toxic kingdom.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Migrating Without King Approval: Never blind-migrate into a controlled kingdom above their published power cap without explicit King permission. Unapproved immigrants are routinely zeroed, targeted on resource tiles, and forced to migrate out.

* Forfeiting Hundreds of Millions in Resources: Do not keep massive un-tokened resource stockpiles in your city before clicking migrate; any resources exceeding your Storehouse capacity limit will be permanently deleted upon arrival.

* Missing the Cross-Season Cap Timer: Relying on Cross-Season migration without a locked King invitation is extremely risky; all 30 spots usually fill within 2 seconds of the server migration window opening.

  • Passport Pages Requirement: Migration requires Passport Pages purchased from the Alliance Shop (600,000 Individual Credits each) or targeted real-money bundles. The total pages needed scale exponentially based on your account's current Individual Power.
  • Target Kingdom Status: To migrate into a kingdom, its status must be listed as Developed (or open for migration). You cannot migrate directly into a kingdom that is currently in an active Lost Kingdom (KvK) battle season or locked in Off-Season snapshot windows.
  • City Hall & Troop Conditions: You must have a City Hall Level 16+, all march queues recalled to city, zero wounded troops inside hospitals, no active alliance membership, and sufficient resource storage capacity (excess resources above storehouse limits are permanently forfeited).

📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

  • Migration Types (Same-Season vs. Cross-Season):
  • Same-Season Migration: Moving between kingdoms within the same KvK Season/Age (e.g., Season of Conquest to Season of Conquest). Subject to standard power caps set by the target King.
  • Cross-Season Migration: Moving from an older season (SoC) back to a younger season (e.g., KvK 2 or KvK 3). Highly restricted by the game engine (typically 30 spots total per kingdom per season via special King invitation).
  • Targeting the Off-Season Window: Migration opens strictly during a kingdom's Off-Season window (the 10 to 14 days between the official end of one KvK and the matchmaking phase of the next).
  • Power Cap Negotiation: King leadership controls the target kingdom's Special Immigration Cap. Contact the King or Migration Officer weeks in advance via mail/Discord to secure an approved spot before burning passports.
  • Power Shedding (Passport Cost Reduction):
  • Purge Un-Needed Troops: Fill your hospital or dismiss excess low-tier (T1–T3) or redundant troops to drop your account below major power thresholds, saving dozens of expensive Passport Pages.
  • De-Equip Gear / Empty Storage: While equipment doesn't cost passports, trimming raw troop power drops your passport bracket (e.g., dropping from 65M to 55M power slashes passport costs significantly).
  • Alliance Credit Stockpiling: Join high-activity alliances months before migrating. Continuously donate to alliance technology and help alliance members to farm millions of Alliance Credits for "free" passports.

⚙️ TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

  • The Unassigned Spot Rush: Uncapped/uncontrolled migration spots open automatically at designated server reset times. If migrating into an open Seed C/D kingdom without a power cap, be logged in with passports ready to click instantly at reset.
  • Farm Account Synchronization: Migrate your primary farm accounts along with your main city during the same Off-Season window to ensure your resource engine remains intact for the upcoming KvK.
  • Kingdom Seed Assessment: Before finalizing migration, review the target kingdom's top 300 power distribution, past KvK records, and Discord organization to avoid migrating into a dead or toxic kingdom.

⚙️ CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

  • Migrating Without King Approval: Never blind-migrate into a controlled kingdom above their published power cap without explicit King permission. Unapproved immigrants are routinely zeroed, targeted on resource tiles, and forced to migrate out.
  • Forfeiting Hundreds of Millions in Resources: Do not keep massive un-tokened resource stockpiles in your city before clicking migrate; any resources exceeding your Storehouse capacity limit will be permanently deleted upon arrival.
  • Missing the Cross-Season Cap Timer: Relying on Cross-Season migration without a locked King invitation is extremely risky; all 30 spots usually fill within 2 seconds of the server migration window opening.

⚔️ KVK PRE-REGISTRATION & MARAUDERS GUIDE

KVK PRE-REGISTRATION & MARAUDERS GUIDE

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

- Pre-KvK Stage 1 (Marauders): The single highest-value PvE event across the current KvK theater. Players hunt Kingdom Map Marauders using Action Points (AP) to earn Marauder Chests containing speedups, resources, and Kingdom Supply Chests.

- Kingdom Supply Chests & Parchments: Marauder Chests drop five distinct types of Parchments (Book, Quill, Ink, Paper, Parchment). Exchanging a full set of 5 distinct Parchments yields a Kingdom Supply Chest containing 3 Universal Legendary Sculptures, high-tier speedups, and massive resource tokens.

- AP Conservation Baseline: Stop spending Action Point recovery bottles weeks before Pre-KvK begins. Every 1,000 AP spent on Marauders yields exponentially more progression value than standard map barbarians.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

- The AP Stockpile Target: F2P and low-spending players should aim to stockpile at least 100,000 to 200,000+ total AP in recovery bottles exclusively for Stage 1.

- Rally vs. Solo March Setup: Marauders must be defeated via single-march attacks or small team hunts; they cannot be summoned via rallies. Deploy 5 Peacekeeping marches simultaneously to minimize AP costs per kill.

- 5-March Peacekeeping Deployment: Run 5 dedicated Peacekeeping primary commanders (such as Lohar, Aethelflaed, Markswoman, Boudica, or Belisarius) with the Trophy Hunter talent maxed to generate free resource packs on every kill.

- AP Discount Stacking: Maximize the Insight talent (-10 AP cost per attack) on all 5 primary Peacekeeping commanders. This reduces the base cost of fighting a Marauder from 50 AP down to 40 AP (and 30 AP on continuous kills).

- Parchment Trading & Exchange: Coordinate within your alliance or kingdom chat to trade duplicate Parchments 1-for-1. Equalizing your parchment counts ensures zero wasted items and maximizes the number of turn-in chests opened.

- VIP & Rune Buffs: Pick up a 10% Action Point Recovery Rune near Holy Sites and ensure your VIP level is as high as possible to accelerate passive AP regeneration throughout Stage 1.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

- The 5-March Swarm Method: Send all 5 Peacekeeping marches to swarm a single Marauder at once. Every march involved consumes AP and receives an independent reward roll, effectively multiplying your parchment drop rate per minute.

- Zone 3 / High-Density Farming: Relocate your city to Zone 3 or densely packed alliance territory where Marauder spawn rates are highest to minimize march travel times between kills.

- Pre-KvK Honor Roll Stage Push: Stage 1 points contribute directly to your kingdom's overall Pre-KvK Honor Roll ranking, unlocking kingdom-wide troop training and damage buffs upon entering the Lost Kingdom map.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

- Dumping AP on Marauder Forts (Stage 2): Avoid spending large AP stashes on Stage 2 Marauder Forts unless your kingdom is competing for a top Honor rank. Stage 1 Marauders offer vastly superior individual speedup and sculpture returns per AP spent.

- Letting Parchments Expire Un-Traded: Never leave unmatched single parchments in your inventory when Stage 1 closes; actively trade all duplicates to claim full Kingdom Supply Chests.

- Using Non-Peacekeeping Commanders: Never hunt Marauders using combat commanders without AP reduction talents; fighting without the Insight talent wastes 25% of your total AP stockpile for zero extra gain.

guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: Dominate the Lost Kingdom frontline, secure strategic landing zones, and lead your alliance to victory during the critical opening hours of KvK! ⚔️ The ultimate Pass 4 Opening Battle Strategy Guide for Rise of Kingdoms. This guide delivers an actionable combat roadmap for controlling Pass 4 on Day 1. Learn how to execute landing zone blocks, manage single-march open-field murderballs in tight bottlenecks, time counter-rallies, and weave alliance flags along protective terrain chokepoints. guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
⚔️ PASS 4 OPENING BATTLE STRATEGY

PASS 4 OPENING BATTLE STRATEGY

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

- Pass 4 Significance: Day 1 of KvK opens Pass 4, connecting outer Home Kingdoms into the contested Zone 4 of the Lost Kingdom map. Whichever kingdom secures territory control around Pass 4 dictates the frontline.

- Garrison & Rally Speccing: Assign your highest-power gear/tech whales to lead primary Rallies and Garrisons. Never allow low-tier or off-meta commanders to lead Pass 4 burn rallies or defensive holds.

- Teleport Locking Mechanics: Upon pass opening, players rush to construct Alliance Flags and teleport cities onto new territory. Blocking enemy city landing zones is just as vital as direct open-field trades.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

- Chokepoint Landing Zone Blocking: Before the pass opens, position non-combat marches or low-tier units across open terrain to block enemy players from dropping targeted teleports near the pass mouth.

- Push Timing (The First 15 Minutes): Initiate main counter-rallies 60 to 90 seconds after the enemy drops their primary flag or rally on Pass 4. Delaying your rally allows your open-field marches to sweep their reinforcements first.

- Territory Flag Weaving: Build alliance flags hugging mountain chokepoints rather than pushing straight into wide open fields, minimizing the number of flag touches the enemy can double-rally simultaneously.

- Single March Field Deployments: F2P and mid-spend players must stick to 1 primary march during open-field Pass 4 brawls. Multi-marching in tight Pass 4 bottlenecks leads to severe AoE melt and massive hospital bills.

- Hospital Healing Cycles: Execute batch healing every 15 minutes utilizing Alliance Helps rather than spending manual speedups on massive hospital queues.

Reddit

* Rally Reinforcement Priority: Reinforce rallies and garrisons using only the requested troop types (e.g., pure Infantry for an Infantry garrison) to preserve active commander talent bonuses.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* The Ball-and-Chain Murderball: Keep your open-field marches clumped tightly behind your kingdom's lead rally. Focus fire on overextended enemy marches attempting to intercept rally reinforcements.

* Rogue Teleport Denial: Deploy peacekeepers or scout units to occupy empty 2x2 grid spaces near your Alliance Center to prevent enemy "zeroing parties" from porting directly into your backline.

* Buffer Flag Sacrifices: Build temporary "sacrificial" flags on contested pass borders to absorb enemy rally momentum while main alliance engineers build reinforced flag chains behind them.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Swarming Enemy AoE Garrisons: Never open-field swarm enemy garrisons or rallies running circular AoE commanders (such as YSG or Zhuge Liang); doing so bleeds massive T4/T5 troops for zero trade value.

* Reinforcing Dead Flags: Do not waste speedups or troops reinforcing an Alliance Flag that is under double-rally with low health; let it burn and reset your defensive line at the next flag.

* Fighting Unshielded Near Open Passes: Never park your city unshielded within 30 tiles of an un-captured Pass 4 gate; enemy rallies can lock onto your city in seconds.

.

guides.content_markdown:
⚔️ RUINS AND ALTAR MECHANICS GUIDE

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

* The Occupation Objective: Ancient Ruins (opens every 36 hours, lasts 2 hours) and Dark Altars (opens every 84 hours, lasts 4 hours) reward continuous individual and alliance Honor Points strictly while allied marches park inside the central capture circle.

* March Limit Restrictions: Each player can only bring 1 active march into the immediate zone surrounding the Ruins or Altar. Multi-marching inside the zone is strictly blocked by game mechanics to balance population caps.

* Ancient Guardians Spawns: Every 15 minutes during the opening window, elite Ancient Guardians spawn around the structure. Defeating these neutral mobs grants high individual Honor, commander XP, and high-tier inventory speedup drops.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

* Pre-Opening March Positioning: Arrive at the zone 10 to 15 minutes prior to the official unlock timer. Form a tight defensive ring with your alliance around the outer perimeter of the capture circle before enemy forces stage their push.

* Tank-Front, Glass-Back Formation: Position heavy tank marches (Infantry defense setups like Scipio/Liu Che or Richard/Constantine) on the outer perimeter facing enemy approach corridors. Squishy damage marches (Zhuge Liang or Nevsky) park safely in the inner circle core.

* Aggressive Funnel Chokeholding: If your alliance dominates the sector, push your frontline past the capture circle to lock down enemy approach paths, allowing your backline players to accumulate uninterrupted occupation points.

* Single-March Setup Efficiency: F2P and low-spend players should deploy strictly their highest-survivability tank/AoE march to maximize field uptime and avoid returning to city due to red-health march recalls.

* Rune & Expansion Stacking: Activate a 20% Army Expansion and grab continuous Health/Defense runic buffs from nearby Holy Sites before entering the zone to boost durability during prolonged team brawls.

* Micro-Step Batch Healing: Keep your march active by taking brief steps back into friendly territory when health drops below 30%, triggering quick batch heals via alliance helps rather than suffering total march wipes.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* Directional AoE Control: Position circular or fan-shaped AoE commanders so their skill cones sweep directly across clustered enemy marches without pulling neutral Guardians early before your alliance is ready to clear them.

* Guardian Tagging Priority: When Ancient Guardians spawn, ensure your march lands at least one direct normal attack hit on every spawn. Hitting a Guardian registers full individual Honor and reward drops upon its death.

* Rotational March Swapping: When your alliance holds total control of the capture circle, rotate damaged marches out of the zone to heal while fresh alliance members step in to maintain max occupation point caps.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Chasing Rogue Enemy Marches: Never break formation to chase down isolated enemy cavalry running around the perimeter; leaving the capture circle forfeits your passive Honor generation and breaks your alliance's defensive murderball.

* Clumping Squishy Marches Forward: Avoid positioning glass-cannon Archer pairings near enemy entry points; enemy cavalry bursts will target exposed backlines and send your march to the hospital in seconds.

* Ignoring Guardian Wave Timers: Do not ignore incoming Guardian waves while fighting enemies. Letting neutral Guardian AoE strikes hit your cluster while engaged with enemy players causes massive unnecessary troop loss.

⚔️ DIPLOMACY & KVK MATCHMAKING GUIDE

## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

* Top 300 Power Baseline: Matchmaking power scores are calculated directly from the combined power of a kingdom's Top 300 Governors. Lower-ranking players outside the top 300 do not impact your kingdom's official matchmaking seed.

* Snapshot Freeze Date: The system takes a hidden data snapshot of your kingdom's top 300 players approximately 1 to 2 weeks before the matchmaking phase officially begins.

* Matchmaking Seeds: Kingdoms are grouped into Seed Tiers based on their relative ranking among competing kingdoms:

* Seed A: Top 10%–15% highest power kingdoms (Whale-heavy, massive T5 field density).

* Seed B: Upper-middle tier (High activity, strong T4/T5 balance).

* Seed C: Lower-middle tier (Manageable field fights, fewer megawhales).

* Seed D: Lowest power tier (Casual kingdoms, lower field density).

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

* Pre-Snapshot Power Management: High-ranking alliances coordinate "Power Caps" prior to snapshot dates, requiring players to hold off on massive troop promotions or troop training until the snapshot locks.

* Diplomatic Coalition Building: King leadership contacts potential alliance kingdoms weeks before KvK drops to form 2-kingdom or 3-kingdom coalitions (Camps) to avoid getting double-teamed on Day 1.

* Migration Target Filtering: Manage incoming target migrations to ensure your kingdom does not accidentally cross the power threshold into a higher Seed Tier right before matchmaking closes.

* Dead Troops and Activity Metrics: System matchmaking algorithms factor historical KvK activity (such as past dead troop counts, Kill Points, and alliance stars) alongside raw power to prevent high-performing kingdoms from seal-clubbing lower seeds.

* Zeroing Inactive Tops: Kingdom leadership systematically zeroes or forces migration on inactive high-power "bloat" accounts that sit in the Top 300 without contributing to KvK wars.

* Title & Buff Synchronization: Pause kingdom-wide power pushes (like Kingdom Training Buffs or Duke titles) during snapshot week to keep seed ratings artificially controlled.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

* Off-Season Troop Purging: Encourage high-power players to burn off excess low-tier troops or un-needed units during Pre-KvK or KvK end-phases to drop overall account bloat.

* Third-Party Scanning Tools: Alliance leadership uses kingdom scanner tools (such as RoKStats or community Discord scanners) to track the real-time top 300 power of neighboring kingdoms in their continent match pool.

* Camp Positioning: In Season of Conquest (SoC), form pre-made 3-kingdom teams to ensure guaranteed ally coordination across border passes.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

* Carrying Inactive Bloat: Carrying 100M+ power players who do not fight inflates your top 300 score, dragging your kingdom into Seed A against active war kingdoms while losing 10% of your operational army.

* Breaking Pre-KvK Diplomatic Pacts: Violating early non-aggression or coalition agreements before Pass 4 opens ruins kingdom reputation, guaranteeing a 3v1 or 7v1 gang-up in future KvK seasons.

* Ignoring Continental Power Creep: Failing to monitor the top 300 stats of the 40 to 60 kingdoms in your migration region leaves leadership blind to sudden seed shifts caused by incoming whale migrations.

⚙️ TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

  • Off-Season Troop Purging: Encourage high-power players to burn off excess low-tier troops or un-needed units during Pre-KvK or KvK end-phases to drop overall account bloat.
  • Third-Party Scanning Tools: Alliance leadership uses kingdom scanner tools (such as RoKStats or community Discord scanners) to track the real-time top 300 power of neighboring kingdoms in their continent match pool.
  • Camp Positioning: In Season of Conquest (SoC), form pre-made 3-kingdom teams to ensure guaranteed ally coordination across border passes.

  • Carrying Inactive Bloat: Carrying 100M+ power players who do not fight inflates your top 300 score, dragging your kingdom into Seed A against active war kingdoms while losing 10% of your operational army.

The ultimate KvK 1 guide

Preparation:

- preserve universal speedups and unopened resource tokens strictly for kvk, so you have speeds ups and tokens to use for healing.

allocate 70%+ of stored Action Point (AP) reserves toward Marauders that will give you high-volume yields of resources and speed ups as well as materials that can help you through kvk 1.

Maintain a verified baseline of 200k troops due to once your account reaches city hall 25 and max commander level at 60, you will be able to run 200k troops as well as making sure you save your 25% and 50% advanced army expansion boost so you can run more troops if needed.

Maintain a verified baseline of gear sets that match your troop type, when specializing in infantry Ensure your governor profile is configured to use infantry gear to better boost your stats and trades.

Best marches for KvK 1:

Valheon telemetry identifies 3 premier field configurations for KvK 1, this is mainly focused on being equal to all and always be a god on the field.

Baibars + Sun Tzu is the strongest epic pair that rules the field against 80% of the legendary commander pairs. Strong AoE that hits many enemies and especially great in murder-ball engagements.

Sun Tzu + YSG is the strongest pair to have a small budget on, they run great out on the field and together they rule the field outranking 95% of the marches out on the field.

CM + YSG is the best pair to run on the kvk 1 field for now, they rule the field being the tankiest and one of the highest damaging marches on the field.

Heliamber:

-You get a heliamber mine that gets heliamber hourly, the heliamber is used to upgrade your heliamber mine to get valor.

-Valor gives you access to hit barbarian forts but where you are way stronger, barbarian forts are very hard to win against. Without minamoto as an F2P or low spender, then it is very difficult to run a rally against a barbarian fort.

-Daybreak trails is like the vengeance gamemode at the start of the kingdom, but its at the start of the kvk, and it gives different rewards as well as heliamber for different stages; the max stage is 300 instead of the 500 in vengeance.

Extra bundles:

- Heliamber season supply which gives 8000 heliamber daily.

- Preserved in amber bundle that gives heliamber and speeds with alliance chest.

- Bounty of the ancients, it's a good gem tier  recharge that gives resources, xp, speed ups and a lot more good items for your account.

flames of war gives you a big source of items to help you be stronger in fights and on the field.

Mountain warfare gives you material choice chests so you can improve your equipment before the big fights.

KvK 1 map:

-Runes are important in kvk, as honor is one of the most important things to staying in your kingdom and also gaining massive rewards.

-Pass fights are the most important fights. You need to access the battlefield before you can fight in it. So it is very important to attend these fights as they are the center of kingdom vs kingdom.

-Kingsland fights are the last and most important part when you have gained the pass, the fights will be critical to see who will end up winning kvk 1.

Tips and tricks for kvk 1:

- Tech is very important, especially Herbal Medicine, due to its extremely hard to get health stats.

- Tech tokens are good and achievable by gathering resources, and by killing barbs, they help you by being able to donate to the kingdom tech which also helps you by giving you honor, and helping the kingdom by being able to upgrade the tech.

- always kill barbarians to gain the extra rewards, the rewards list is incredible when it comes to being in kvk 1, you should always be sure to go through all rewards and get everything possible.

-never fight 1v1, always fight as a team. You can sometimes be caught in times where you can fight a 1v1, and in that instant, then you would fight. But the truth is being the runner on the field is way smarter than being the chaser, cause you choose the way you want to fight and go.

-follow leadership orders when they are said, many people tend to go their own route to chase kp, but the fact is that if you stay together, then you will gain 3x more kp than if you always ran your own kvk.

guides.title: War Guide
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: Master the battlefields of the Lost Kingdom! ⚔️ The definitive combat and mechanics guide for Rise of Kingdoms. Learn the deep math behind rage generation (hitting the 220-cap), micro-tactics like city hopping and march stacking, group strategies like the "Murder Ball," and a complete zone-by-zone roadmap to dominating your very first KvK season.
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
# War

- During KvK, focus your attacks on enemy kingdoms only. Avoid fighting players from your own kingdom.

- Internal conflicts and civil wars can severely slow down account growth, especially in the early stages of the game, so stay out of them whenever possible.

# Field Fighting

Before heading into battle, make sure everything is set up correctly to get the most value from your marches:

- Verify your equipment, talents, and armaments (KvK2) are properly configured.

- Activate a 50% Defense Buff whenever possible. If unavailable, use an Attack Buff or Expansion Buff.

- When using an Expansion Buff, fill your march to maximum capacity and keep it to a single troop type.

- Equip a city skin that benefits your troop type if you own one.

- Review your Commander View tab before joining the fight.

- Pick up a combat rune before fighting, or a healing rune if you're planning to heal troops.

- After healing, remember to grab a combat rune again before returning to battle.

- Obtain a fighting title if one is available, although these are often prioritized for rally and garrison leaders.

- Check the newspaper buffs to ensure you're not missing any active bonuses.

- Follow alliance markers and stay with the main fighting group ("the ball") to maximize your Kill Points.

- Avoid chasing enemy marches across the map, as this usually lowers your efficiency and reduces potential KP gains.

# 🫟 Rage

# Rage Generation Mechanics

Before modifiers such as Silent Trial are applied, the theoretical maximum rage generation per turn is 220 rage.

## Base Rage Generation

### Normal Attacks

Attacking the target you are directly focused on generates:

- 86 rage per turn

### Counterattacks

When other marches attack your march while you are not directly targeting them, you generate:

- 16 rage per turn, per attacking march

# Shared Talent Rage Sources

## Rage from Normal Attacks

### +9 Rage per Normal Attack

The following talents provide an additional 9 rage per normal attack:

- Undying Fury (Infantry and Cavalry Trees)

- Razor Sharp (Archer Tree)

- Burning Blood (Skill and Support Trees)

### +25 Rage per Normal Attack

The following talent activates when troop count falls below 30%:

- Desperate Elegy (Defense Tree)

## Rage from Counterattacks

### +6 Rage per Counterattack

The following talents provide additional rage from counterattacks:

- Hidden Wrath (Leadership Tree)

- Nowhere to Turn (Garrison and Versatility Trees)

- Burning Blood (Attack and Defense Trees)

# Unique Talents

## Rejuvenate

- Skill Tree:

- Grants +60 rage when using an active skill

- Support Tree:

- Grants +150 rage when using an active skill

## Feral Nature

- Provides a:

- 10% chance for normal attacks to generate an additional 100 rage

# Commander Skill Rage Sources

## Charge — Pelagius

- Grants:

- 100 rage per active skill use

## Divine Revelation — Joan of Arc

- Grants:

- 50 rage per second for 4 seconds

- Applies to:

Your own march

- Up to 4 nearby allied marches

## Rage Proc Skills

The following commander skills provide:

- 10% chance for normal attacks to generate 100 rage

Included skills:

- Art of Archery — Yi Seong-Gye

- National Hero — Hermann

- Lofty Ambition — Cao Cao

## Military Lifestyle — Genghis Khan

- Grants:

- 25 rage per counterattack

- Activates when troop count falls below 50%

# Equipment-Based Rage Generation

## Karuak’s War Drums (Accessory)

- Provides:

- 30% chance on normal attacks to grant:

50 rage to your own march

- 50 rage to up to 2 nearby allied marches

# Additional Notes

- Once the primary commander reaches the required rage threshold for their active skill, the skill is cast one turn later.

- On the turn following the primary commander’s active skill activation, the secondary commander will cast their active skill.

- Any action that triggers a battle report will reset your rage to 0.

## Practical Tip

- Frequently switching targets during large fights can reduce the likelihood of triggering battle reports while attacking multiple marches, helping preserve rage cycling efficiency.

# 🏙️ City hopping

# Hopping

During war, players often relocate their cities so they are positioned closely together, minimizing gaps between alliances. This allows more players to stay within the same combat area instead of having to teleport long distances back into the fight.

A useful movement mechanic in this context is known as “hopping.”

## What is Hopping?

Hopping is a fast repositioning technique where a player temporarily sends a troop to a target location (such as a resource point or city) and immediately redirects it elsewhere.

This allows the troop to effectively “reset” its movement path, enabling instant disengagement and rapid relocation without waiting for full travel time.

## Why It Is Useful

- Saves significant travel time during active warfare

- Allows quick repositioning between objectives

- Helps maintain uptime in fast-moving battles

- Can be enhanced by talents or skills that increase movement speed after leaving nodes or structures

In practical terms, hopping is a mobility optimization technique that helps players stay actively involved in fights while minimizing downtime between movements.

# ⭕ Murder ball

# Murder Balls (Group Combat Strategy)

## Part 1 — Core Concept

In large-scale alliance warfare, fighting as a coordinated group provides a significant tactical advantage. Even when facing stronger opponents, numerical coordination can outweigh individual power differences.

The key principle is simple: concentrating more allied marches in one area increases overall combat effectiveness. Even if the opposing force has greater total strength on the field, a well-organized group can overwhelm isolated or uncoordinated enemies through concentrated damage and reinforcement.

## Part 2 — What is a Murder Ball?

A Murder Ball refers to a tightly grouped formation of alliance marches moving and fighting together as a single coordinated unit.

### Formation & Leadership

- The formation location is typically marked by R4/R5 leadership

- Players are expected to follow assigned markers without delay

- Tight positioning is essential for maximizing protection and damage output

### Key Principles

- The tighter the formation, the stronger and safer the group becomes

- The group is continuously moving between objectives

- Maintaining pace with the group is critical—lagging behind reduces effectiveness and survivability

### Practical Viewing Tip

On mobile, it is often beneficial to slightly zoom out on the battlefield. This reduces marches into smaller icons (often diamond-like shapes), making it easier to:

- Identify enemy targets within the cluster

- Detect overextended allied marches

- Maintain awareness of formation integrity

## Part 3 — Combat Execution

When engaging in open-field combat within a Murder Ball, focus is placed on coordinated targeting and synergy between commanders.

### Key Objectives

- Prioritize high-value or vulnerable enemy commanders

- Maintain constant group movement and positioning

- Ensure alliance buffs and bonuses are actively utilized within the formation

Effective Murder Ball combat relies on discipline, timing, and alignment with alliance leadership directives, rather than individual engagement.

# 🏇 Rally system

# Rally System Overview

The term “Rally” is commonly used throughout the game, particularly during war and alliance-based activities. Understanding how rallies function is essential for both PvE and PvP gameplay.

# What is a Rally?

A Rally is a coordinated attack formed by multiple governors combining their troops under a single rally leader.

The player initiating the rally determines:

- The target

- The commander composition

- The troop type

- The launch timing

The maximum rally capacity is determined primarily by the level of the player’s Castle building. Higher Castle levels allow more troops to participate in the rally.

Rallies are one of the primary methods used to defeat or attack objectives such as:

- Flags

- Fortresses

- Holy Sites

- Passes

- Barbarian Forts

- Enemy cities

- Enemy rallies

- Other strategic structures

# Types of Rallies

## Normal Rally

A Normal Rally is launched with the purpose of destroying or capturing enemy objectives.

Common targets include:

- Enemy structures

- Flags

- Fortresses

- Cities

- Strategic objectives

This is the most common type of rally used during war and kingdom conflicts.

## Counter Rally

A Counter Rally is launched specifically to destroy an enemy rally that is attacking an allied structure or objective.

The purpose of a counter rally is to:

- Relieve pressure on allied defenses

- Eliminate enemy rally presence

- Protect key structures from being captured or damaged

Counter rallies are a critical defensive tactic during large-scale warfare.

## Carrier Rally

A Carrier Rally is a rally designed to safely transport primary fighting marches through dangerous or enemy-controlled territory.

This method is useful because:

- Marches inside the rally cannot be directly targeted while traveling

- It increases the likelihood of safely reaching contested objectives or frontline battle areas

Carrier rallies are commonly used during KvK and large alliance wars where movement through hostile territory is necessary.

## Tracker Rally

A Tracker Rally is an unreleased or inactive-style rally concept intended solely to monitor the location of a target over an extended period.

Key characteristics:

- Typically set for 8 hours

- Used for tracking enemy movement or activity

- Not intended for actual combat engagement

The primary purpose is information gathering and target monitoring rather than initiating an attack.

# 🚸 March Stacking

# March Stacking

March stacking is a key field combat technique used in large-scale open-field battles, particularly during alliance “ball” fights. Despite its importance, many players are unfamiliar with how it works, even though the execution is relatively simple.

## What is March Stacking?

March stacking is a positioning method where multiple of your marches are tightly grouped together before engaging a target, allowing them to move and attack as a unified cluster rather than as separate units.

## How to Perform March Stacking

- Enable Quick Command for your marches.

- Deploy all available marches simultaneously, depending on how many you have active.

- Using Quick Command, rapidly tap or switch between positions side-to-side to align your marches tightly together.

- Continue adjusting until your marches appear fully stacked and closely grouped as one compact formation.

Once properly executed, your marches will be positioned in a tight formation, ready to engage a target as a single coordinated unit.

## How It Works in Combat

When a stacked formation engages an enemy target:

- Your marches will remain closely grouped instead of spreading out individually

- They will behave more like a single concentrated strike rather than multiple scattered attacks

- This allows you to focus damage efficiently within enemy formations, especially inside large “murder ball” fights

## Strategic Advantage

The main benefit of march stacking is increased combat efficiency in crowded battlefield situations:

- Prevents your marches from dispersing randomly around a single enemy target

- Improves focus fire within dense enemy formations

- Increases the chance of eliminating key enemy marches caught within the opposing ball

- Enhances coordination with alliance-wide group fighting strategies

In essence, march stacking helps your forces operate as a compact, high-impact unit rather than fragmented individual marches, making it especially effective during large alliance engagements.

# ⚔️ KvK 1

# Kingdom vs Kingdom 1: Endless War (KvK1)

Around 80 days after a kingdom’s creation, the pre-KvK phase begins. Approximately six days later, the Lost Kingdom opens, marking the start of Kingdom vs Kingdom Season 1.

# Overview of KvK1

In KvK1, your kingdom is matched against a regional group of four kingdoms. These are the kingdoms directly bordering the Lost Kingdom map, forming your KvK bracket.

# Kingdom Positioning on the Map

Your kingdom’s starting position in KvK1 is determined by its numerical order within the region:

- 1st kingdom in region → Top-left province

- 2nd kingdom in region → Top-right province

- 3rd kingdom in region → Bottom-right province

- 4th kingdom in region → Bottom-left province

# Lost Kingdom Zones

## Zone 4 (Starting Zone)

Zone 4 is the initial entry area for all kingdoms. It is considered a relatively protected zone due to Pass 5 restrictions, which prevent external kingdoms from entering.

### Key Early Objectives

- Crusader Camp

The first major objective to capture upon entering the Lost Kingdom.

- Ruined Crusader Fortress (RCF)

Typically taken around two days after the Crusader Camp.

This structure is highly important because its capture unlocks Past Glory stages.

Unlocking Past Glory allows kingdoms to:

- Choose kingdom colors

- Teleport freely within kingdom territory

- Improve strategic positioning for future battles

This becomes essential for all later phases of KvK.

## Ancient Ruins (First Cross-Kingdom Contact)

Once Pass 4 is secured, the Ancient Ruins area becomes accessible. This is the first location where direct contact between kingdoms occurs.

### Key Information

- This is typically the first real PvP encounter in KvK1

- After a Chronicle is completed, the Ancient Ruins open after 12 hours and remain open for 1 hour

- For the remainder of KvK, they open every 39 hours and stay open for 1 hour

## Zone 5 (Mid-Game Territory)

After Pass 5 is secured, Zone 5 becomes accessible.

### Features

- Access to higher-level barbarians (Levels 31–36)

- Improved resource node quality compared to Zone 4

- Temporary peace zone in early KvK stages

Later in KvK, this zone may become contested once additional passes are opened and enemy kingdoms gain access.

### Key Structure

- Circles (strategic objectives within the zone)

## Zone 6 (Major Combat Zone)

Zone 6 is one of the most important zones in KvK1 and often marks the first large-scale territorial wars of the season.

### Key Considerations

- Active participation is critical for earning DKP and KvK rewards

- Players are often assessed on individual performance during this stage

- This phase reveals account strength and highlights areas for improvement

### Key Structures

- Hieron

- Sanctuary

## Kingsland (Zone 7)

Kingsland represents the final and most important battlefield of KvK1.

### Important Notes

- After securing Pass 7, kingdoms cannot immediately build flags or teleport into Kingsland

- Initial combat focuses on control of the Altar of Darkness

- There are four Altars of Darkness available for contest

### Altar of Darkness Rules

- Each altar opens 12 hours after the previous Chronicle is completed

- For the remainder of KvK, altars open every 84 hours and remain open for 2 hours

- After approximately 7–9 days, kingdoms gain the ability to build flags and engage in full territorial warfare

## Final Objective: The Ziggurat

- The ultimate structure in KvK1 is the Great Ziggurat

- The kingdom that controls it at the end of KvK earns a permanent star on its alliance banner

- This marks the winning kingdom of the season

# Summary

KvK1 progresses through escalating zones of conflict:

- Zone 4: Preparation and early objectives

- Zone 5: Resource expansion and preparation for war

- Zone 6: First major kingdom-scale battles

- Zone 7 (Kingsland): Final decisive war for victory

Each phase increases in intensity and strategic importance, culminating in the final fight for the Ziggurat.

In large-scale alliance warfare, fighting as a coordinated group provides a significant tactical advantage. Even when facing stronger opponents, numerical coordination can outweigh individual power differences.

The key principle is simple: concentrating more allied marches in one area increases overall combat effectiveness. Even if the opposing force has greater total strength on the field, a well-organized group can overwhelm isolated or uncoordinated enemies through concentrated damage and reinforcement.

Part 2 — What is a Murder Ball?

A Murder Ball refers to a tightly grouped formation of alliance marches moving and fighting together as a single coordinated unit.

Formation & Leadership

  • The formation location is typically marked by R4/R5 leadership
  • Players are expected to follow assigned markers without delay
  • Tight positioning is essential for maximizing protection and damage output

Key Principles

  • The tighter the formation, the stronger and safer the group becomes
  • The group is continuously moving between objectives
  • Maintaining pace with the group is critical—lagging behind reduces effectiveness and survivability

Practical Viewing Tip

On mobile, it is often beneficial to slightly zoom out on the battlefield. This reduces marches into smaller icons (often diamond-like shapes), making it easier to:

  • Identify enemy targets within the cluster
  • Detect overextended allied marches
  • Maintain awareness of formation integrity

Part 3 — Combat Execution

When engaging in open-field combat within a Murder Ball, focus is placed on coordinated targeting and synergy between commanders.

Key Objectives

  • Prioritize high-value or vulnerable enemy commanders
  • Maintain constant group movement and positioning
  • Ensure alliance buffs and bonuses are actively utilized within the formation

Effective Murder Ball combat relies on discipline, timing, and alignment with alliance leadership directives, rather than individual engagement.

🏇 Rally system

Rally System Overview

The term “Rally” is commonly used throughout the game, particularly during war and alliance-based activities. Understanding how rallies function is essential for both PvE and PvP gameplay.

What is a Rally?

A Rally is a coordinated attack formed by multiple governors combining their troops under a single rally leader.

The player initiating the rally determines:

  • The target
  • The commander composition
  • The troop type
  • The launch timing

The maximum rally capacity is determined primarily by the level of the player’s Castle building. Higher Castle levels allow more troops to participate in the rally.

Rallies are one of the primary methods used to defeat or attack objectives such as:

  • Flags
  • Fortresses
  • Holy Sites
  • Passes
  • Barbarian Forts
  • Enemy cities
  • Enemy rallies
  • Other strategic structures

Types of Rallies

Normal Rally

A Normal Rally is launched with the purpose of destroying or capturing enemy objectives.

Common targets include:

  • Enemy structures
  • Flags
  • Fortresses
  • Cities
  • Strategic objectives

This is the most common type of rally used during war and kingdom conflicts.

Counter Rally

A Counter Rally is launched specifically to destroy an enemy rally that is attacking an allied structure or objective.

The purpose of a counter rally is to:

  • Relieve pressure on allied defenses
  • Eliminate enemy rally presence
  • Protect key structures from being captured or damaged

Counter rallies are a critical defensive tactic during large-scale warfare.

Carrier Rally

A Carrier Rally is a rally designed to safely transport primary fighting marches through dangerous or enemy-controlled territory.

This method is useful because:

  • Marches inside the rally cannot be directly targeted while traveling
  • It increases the likelihood of safely reaching contested objectives or frontline battle areas

Carrier rallies are commonly used during KvK and large alliance wars where movement through hostile territory is necessary.

Tracker Rally

A Tracker Rally is an unreleased or inactive-style rally concept intended solely to monitor the location of a target over an extended period.

Key characteristics:

  • Typically set for 8 hours
  • Used for tracking enemy movement or activity
  • Not intended for actual combat engagement

The primary purpose is information gathering and target monitoring rather than initiating an attack.

🚸 March Stacking

March Stacking

March stacking is a key field combat technique used in large-scale open-field battles, particularly during alliance “ball” fights. Despite its importance, many players are unfamiliar with how it works, even though the execution is relatively simple.

What is March Stacking?

March stacking is a positioning method where multiple of your marches are tightly grouped together before engaging a target, allowing them to move and attack as a unified cluster rather than as separate units.

How to Perform March Stacking

  • Enable Quick Command for your marches.
  • Deploy all available marches simultaneously, depending on how many you have active.
  • Using Quick Command, rapidly tap or switch between positions side-to-side to align your marches tightly together.
  • Continue adjusting until your marches appear fully stacked and closely grouped as one compact formation.

Once properly executed, your marches will be positioned in a tight formation, ready to engage a target as a single coordinated unit.

How It Works in Combat

When a stacked formation engages an enemy target:

  • Your marches will remain closely grouped instead of spreading out individually
  • They will behave more like a single concentrated strike rather than multiple scattered attacks
  • This allows you to focus damage efficiently within enemy formations, especially inside large “murder ball” fights

Strategic Advantage

The main benefit of march stacking is increased combat efficiency in crowded battlefield situations:

  • Prevents your marches from dispersing randomly around a single enemy target
  • Improves focus fire within dense enemy formations
  • Increases the chance of eliminating key enemy marches caught within the opposing ball
  • Enhances coordination with alliance-wide group fighting strategies

In essence, march stacking helps your forces operate as a compact, high-impact unit rather than fragmented individual marches, making it especially effective during large alliance engagements.

⚔️ KvK 1

Kingdom vs Kingdom 1: Endless War (KvK1)

Around 80 days after a kingdom’s creation, the pre-KvK phase begins. Approximately six days later, the Lost Kingdom opens, marking the start of Kingdom vs Kingdom Season 1.

Overview of KvK1

In KvK1, your kingdom is matched against a regional group of four kingdoms. These are the kingdoms directly bordering the Lost Kingdom map, forming your KvK bracket.

Kingdom Positioning on the Map

Your kingdom’s starting position in KvK1 is determined by its numerical order within the region:

  • 1st kingdom in region → Top-left province
  • 2nd kingdom in region → Top-right province
  • 3rd kingdom in region → Bottom-right province
  • 4th kingdom in region → Bottom-left province

Lost Kingdom Zones

Zone 4 (Starting Zone)

Zone 4 is the initial entry area for all kingdoms. It is considered a relatively protected zone due to Pass 5 restrictions, which prevent external kingdoms from entering.

Key Early Objectives

  • Crusader Camp

The first major objective to capture upon entering the Lost Kingdom.

  • Ruined Crusader Fortress (RCF)

Typically taken around two days after the Crusader Camp.

This structure is highly important because its capture unlocks Past Glory stages.

Unlocking Past Glory allows kingdoms to:

  • Choose kingdom colors
  • Teleport freely within kingdom territory
  • Improve strategic positioning for future battles

This becomes essential for all later phases of KvK.

Ancient Ruins (First Cross-Kingdom Contact)

Once Pass 4 is secured, the Ancient Ruins area becomes accessible. This is the first location where direct contact between kingdoms occurs.

Key Information

  • This is typically the first real PvP encounter in KvK1
  • After a Chronicle is completed, the Ancient Ruins open after 12 hours and remain open for 1 hour
  • For the remainder of KvK, they open every 39 hours and stay open for 1 hour

Zone 5 (Mid-Game Territory)

After Pass 5 is secured, Zone 5 becomes accessible.

Features

  • Access to higher-level barbarians (Levels 31–36)
  • Improved resource node quality compared to Zone 4
  • Temporary peace zone in early KvK stages

Later in KvK, this zone may become contested once additional passes are opened and enemy kingdoms gain access.

Key Structure

  • Circles (strategic objectives within the zone)

Zone 6 (Major Combat Zone)

Zone 6 is one of the most important zones in KvK1 and often marks the first large-scale territorial wars of the season.

Key Considerations

  • Active participation is critical for earning DKP and KvK rewards
  • Players are often assessed on individual performance during this stage
  • This phase reveals account strength and highlights areas for improvement

Key Structures

  • Hieron
  • Sanctuary

Kingsland (Zone 7)

Kingsland represents the final and most important battlefield of KvK1.

Important Notes

  • After securing Pass 7, kingdoms cannot immediately build flags or teleport into Kingsland
  • Initial combat focuses on control of the Altar of Darkness
  • There are four Altars of Darkness available for contest

Altar of Darkness Rules

  • Each altar opens 12 hours after the previous Chronicle is completed
  • For the remainder of KvK, altars open every 84 hours and remain open for 2 hours
  • After approximately 7–9 days, kingdoms gain the ability to build flags and engage in full territorial warfare

Final Objective: The Ziggurat

  • The ultimate structure in KvK1 is the Great Ziggurat
  • The kingdom that controls it at the end of KvK earns a permanent star on its alliance banner
  • This marks the winning kingdom of the season

Summary

KvK1 progresses through escalating zones of conflict:

  • Zone 4: Preparation and early objectives
  • Zone 5: Resource expansion and preparation for war
  • Zone 6: First major kingdom-scale battles
  • Zone 7 (Kingsland): Final decisive war for victory

Each phase increases in intensity and strategic importance, culminating in the final fight for the Ziggurat.

guides.title: Farm Account Management
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: Fuel your main account, eliminate resource bottlenecks, and master multi-account management without burning out! 🌾 The ultimate Farm Account Creation & Management Guide for Rise of Kingdoms. This guide delivers a complete roadmap for building and running high-yield farm accounts. Learn how to rush City Hall 17 and 22 for maximum march queues, optimize civilization picks and T1 Siege production, and level core gatherers to Level 37 for peak output. Discover crucial strategies for upgrading Trading Posts to minimize transfer taxes, managing dedicated farm alliances, and avoiding anti-cheat flags—keeping your main account continuously stocked with resources for war!
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

- City Hall Progression Milestones: Rush your farm account's City Hall straight to CH 17 to unlock 4 march queues, and ultimately CH 22 for all 5 march queues.

- Civilization Selection: Start as France for Joan of Arc (gathering buff) and the 3% general gathering speed boost, then switch to Byzantium (10% Stone) or Rome (10% Food) based on your main's resource needs.

- T1 Siege Production: Produce T1 Siege (Battering Rams) exclusively. They are cheap, fast to build, have massive load capacities, and cost almost nothing in hospital fees if attacked on resource tiles.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

- Trading Post Upgrades: Maximize your Trading Post level on every farm account as early as possible. A low-level Trading Post imposes up to a 25% tax rate on transfers, wasting millions in resources.

- Account Linking Setup: Create farms on separate character slots within the same kingdom (or use secondary email/social logins) so you can run multi-instance emulators on PC for simultaneous gathering.

- Dedicated Gathering Commanders: Level core gathering commanders (Constance, Sárka, Gaius, Seondeok, Cleo, Ishida) to Level 37 to unlock the full gathering talent tree without wasting extra XP.

- Alliance Territory Gathering: Place your farm accounts in a dedicated farm alliance (or sister alliance) that controls territory with high-level resource nodes and active alliance resource pits.

- Transfer Tax Minimization: Always transfer resources via direct Trading Post transport rather than city attacks; city raiding incurs heavy troop loss, hospital costs, and potential anti-cheat flags.

- Resource Specialization: Assign specific farms to dedicated resource types (e.g., Farm 1 focuses strictly on Gold/Food, Farm 2 focuses on Wood/Stone) to maximize commander skill synergies.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

- Daily AP Utilization: Spend your farm's free daily Action Points on map barbarians during events to stock up inventory speedup chests and additional resource tokens.

- Courier Station Discount Buys: Check the Courier Station on your farms daily to buy resource tokens and gathering speedup items using raw, uncollected city resources.

- VIP 6 Baseline: Get your farm accounts to VIP 6 as quickly as possible using free gems from events to permanently unlock the 2nd building queue and passive gathering boosts.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

- Training High-Tier Combat Units: Never train T3 or T4 troops on farm accounts; they drain high amounts of food/gold in upkeep and waste speedups better used on technology upgrades.

- Rushing CH 25 Early: Do not waste valuable resources pushing a farm past City Hall 22 early on; CH 22 already provides 5 full gathering marches at a fraction of the cost.

- Transferring During Anti-Bot Flags: Avoid sending massive, rapid resource transfers on brand new accounts without daily activity, as this can trigger automated resource removal flags.

guides.title: Gathering Talent Tree — Tactical Dossier
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: Master the ideal talent setups, optimize leveling paths, and maximize your daily resource yields across every node! 🌾 The ultimate Gathering Commander Talent Trees & Leveling Guide for Rise of Kingdoms. This guide outlines how to build and level your gathering commanders for peak efficiency. Learn why Level 37 is the critical milestone for Superior Gathering, how Level 40 unlocks Modified Axle for maximum return speed, and how primary-only talent rules dictate your pairings. Discover zero-cost XP leveling tricks through Guardian runs, ideal secondary pairings with commanders like Constance for completion bonuses, and essential safety talents to keep your gatherers fast, safe, and productive!
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

- Commander Level Thresholds: Level 37 is the absolute baseline for all primary gatherers to unlock Superior Gathering, which grants maximum speed across all node types. Level 40 is the endgame goal to pick up Modified Axle for maximum March Speed.

- Primary-Only Talent Rule: Only the talents on your Primary Commander are active during gathering runs. The talents of your Secondary Commander do not apply—only their skill levels boost performance.

- Troop Load vs. March Speed: Siege units possess the highest load capacity per unit in the game, making T1 Siege the most cost-effective troop choice for clearing high-level resource nodes without inflating hospital costs.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

- Universal Level 37 Base Build: Rush straight to the top node of the Gathering tree to max Superior Gathering (3/3). From there, fill out node-specific nodes based on your commander's natural specialization (Stone, Gold, Food, or Wood).

- Level 40 Max Efficiency Path: After hitting Level 37, spend your remaining 3 talent points directly into Modified Axle (3/3) in the Integration/Mobility tree (or leftover base gathering nodes) to increase march speed when returning to city with full loads.

- Secondary March Pairings: Pair specialized primary gatherers (e.g., Seondeok for Gold) with high-yield secondary gatherers (like Constance or Joan of Arc) to secure extra resource packs upon node completion.

- Node Clearance Bonus: Maximize The More The Merrier (3/3) in the talent tree to gain an extra 6% resource bonus delivered directly to your inventory bag upon fully clearing a resource deposit.

- March Speed Out of Nodes: Unlock Swiftness (2/2) and Hasty Departure (1/1) to grant your gathering marches massive temporary movement speed bursts when exiting resource tiles to evade enemy tile-hunters.

- Load Capacity Allocation: Take Armed to the Teeth (3/3) if gathering with non-siege marches during war zones, but rely primarily on Gathering Mastery nodes to naturally expand march carrying capacity.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

- Leveling Gatherers via Guardians: Never waste generic Knowledge Tomes on farm commanders past Level 20. Send your gathering commanders as secondary commanders to daily Holy Site Guardian runs to level them to 37 completely free.

- Zone 3 Node Targeting: Park your farm marches near high-tier nodes in Zone 3 or KvK maps; higher-level nodes feature larger total resource pools, keeping your gatherers operating at peak efficiency for hours.

- Kingdom & Alliance Buff Stacking: Activate a 24-Hour 80% Gathering Boost item alongside active Alliance Territory gathering buffs (+25%) before dispatching your fully-specced gatherers overnight.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

- Pushing Gatherers Past Level 40: Avoid spending XP to level gathering commanders to Level 60; talent points past Level 40 grant negligible utility for resource gathering and waste millions of XP better spent on combat commanders.

- Leaving Nodes Partially Cleared: Never abandon a resource node with a few thousand resources remaining. Failing to clear a node prevents new high-level nodes from spawning in your alliance territory.

- Gathering with High-Tier Combat Units: Avoid sending T4 or T5 combat troops to gather during KvK; if your tile gets attacked, repairing high-tier units drains massive amounts of gold and speedups.

guides.title: Gem Gathering Guide
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: Tired of wasting precious march time every time your gatherers return home after a single gem node? 💎  Discover how to use pass-locking across the current KvK theater to keep your gatherers out in Zone 2 hopping from node to node effortlessly! Learn the exact setup, march load requirements, and key commander pairings to safely maximize your daily gem yields while keeping your account safe.
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
GEM GATHERING GUIDE

CurlyGaming X Valheon Citadel

This guide is for all players, Early game through SOC, this method can be used for all accounts F2P to P2W.

This guide is in an SOC HK account however this works in any KVK and account that has unlocked level 2 passes in your home kingdom!

Most players send out the gathers individually, and gather 1 node at a time closest to their city with a couple of marches.

This method works, however it is super inefficient and is using up more of your time than needed!

The best method to gem farming is by locking your march outside of passes. (Shown in CurlyGaming Youtube video)

•In this method you are going to send out 1-5 marches from your city in zone 3 to each zone in zone 2.

•make sure your marches have lots of troops able to farm up to 1,000+ gems at a time (80k+)

•When your marches arrive at the level 3 passes leave and go to each allaince controlling the pass to get your march through.

•now Ensure your governor profile is configured to do not return to an allaince controlling a level 3 pass otherwise your marches will return after the gem node is finished farming!

• if you have done the above step correctly then you will see that after finishing a gem node your march has fully stopped where the former node was. This meaning you can do a few nodes, go back to scrolling CurlyGaming YouTube shorts, log back in do some more, and not have to 24/7 grind the gem nodes and worry about them returning to your city.

Reality/gem botting:

•do not compare your gem farming, or gem farming reports to any other player, the sad reality is lots of players are now using gem bots. That is somewhat being banned by Lilith. These gem bots offer 4k gems a day for each march crazy stats. For 1 it is morally wrong and for 2 the chance of being banned for this is the highest it’s ever been.

guides.title: Honor Points Farming — Tactical Dossier
guides.summary: Valheon Strategic Dossier: Maxize your KvK leaderboard rankings, unlock top-tier reward milestones, and master efficient Honor Point farming! 🏆 The ultimate KvK Honor Point Farming Guide for Rise of Kingdoms. This guide breaks down the core mechanics of accumulating personal and alliance Honor across the Lost Kingdom map. Learn how to never miss Ancient Ruins and Dark Altars schedules, maximize barbarian AoE chaining for high Honor yields at low AP costs, and deploy 5-march swarms in high-density zones. Discover crucial strategies for territory gathering, AP bottle allocation, and alliance fort rallies to push your ranking and claim exclusive city skins and legendary sculptures!
guides.author: Valheon Strategic Intelligence
guides.content_markdown:
## ⚙️ Core System Mechanics & Quantitative Baseline

- Honor Point Sources: Honor Points are accumulated through four primary activities: occupying Holy Sites (Ruins/Altars), barbarian hunting (single kills & AoE chaining), destroying Barbarian Forts, and gathering resources within the Lost Kingdom.

- Alliance vs. Individual Honor Dual-Track: Individual Honor unlocks personal reward milestones (up to 130,000+ points for City Skins and Legendary Sculptures). Alliance Honor drives your alliance’s overall rank on the KvK leaderboard for kingdom-wide buffs.

- Level Scaling: High-level barbarians (Level 36–40–45+ depending on KvK season) yield significantly more Honor Points per kill than low-level ones. Always push forward into higher zones as passes open.

## 📋 Valheon Tactical Execution Protocol

- Ruins and Dark Altars Priority: Ancient Ruins open every 36 hours (lasting 2 hours) and Dark Altars open every 84 hours (lasting 4 hours). Parking a march inside the capture circle yields passive Honor Points per minute—never miss a schedule window.

- Barbarian AoE Chaining: Use circular AoE commanders (like Sun Tzu, YSG, or Zhuge Liang) to pull multiple barbarians into your main target. Damaging adjacent barbarians rewards full Honor Points for 0 extra AP spent per chained target.

- 5-March Simultaneous Hunting: When active, deploy 5 Peacekeeping/AoE marches into high-density zones. Swarming a single barbarian with 5 marches rewards independent Honor rolls for each march involved.

- AP Discount Talent Utilization: Maximize the Insight talent (-10 AP cost per attack) on all primary Peacekeeping commanders to drop continuous barbarian kill costs to 30 AP per march.

- Gathering Node Honor Integration: Send gathering marches exclusively to Level 6+ resource nodes located inside alliance territory. Completely clearing a high-tier node yields bonus individual and alliance Honor upon completion.

- Action Point Bottle Allocation: Save your heavy Action Point recovery bottle stockpiles for high-level barbarian sectors (Zone 5, Zone 6, and the Lost Temple / Kingsland area) where Honor payouts per AP spent reach their peak.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

- Ruins Dual-March Strategy: If your alliance controls the Ancient Ruins uncontested, send two distinct marches (or assist alliance members) to occupy the circle to maximize individual Honor gains during the 2-hour window.
